differences.description: The Android Adapter dispatches Channel results and events through the Android main thread.
The iOS Adapter dispatches Channel results and events through the main actor or main queue.
The Android Adapter creates transfer files under a plugin-owned application-private cache transfer root.
The iOS Adapter creates transfer files under a plugin-owned application-private cache transfer root.

boundaries.description: Flutter Engine attachment ended and cannot retain Bridge-owned native resources.
Activity or ViewController owner ended while the Engine attachment may remain alive.

dataClassifications.description: Capability-created Session and Media registry identifiers.
Current camera and control support reported by the module.
Minimum metadata for captured media and its lease.
Bounded upright JPEG bytes and the minimum metadata required to display and validate them.
Wire envelope correlation and discriminator fields.
Capability V3 surfaces, factories, targets, sources, renderers, bindings, ownership and diagnostics are Native lifecycle artifacts, not Wire data.
Adapter-created export handle, temporary file URI and expiry for one scoped materialized transfer.
Bounded metadata for the materialized media file copied by the Adapter-owned sink.
Opaque request correlation used only by the originating Flutter client to dismiss its active native presentation.

policies.description: Media transfer is limited to classified metadata, opaque handles, and the declared sanitized bounded thumbnail copy.
Only Capability-created opaque handles may cross the Channel.
Every Map and field is declared by the Wire Contract.
Unknown envelope, payload, and error detail fields are rejected.
Error details use typed closed value sets and never echo unknown input.
Logs redact handles, paths, bytes, metadata, payloads, request IDs, owner generations, and exceptions.
RenderTarget Adapter, owner generation, attachment result, revocation event, SDK object, and native preview scope are never encoded in a method, event, payload, or field mapping.
Capability V3 surface factories, conformances, mount endpoints, backing targets, sources, renderers, bindings and owner scopes never receive a Wire field, payload, method, event or fallback.

Native render diagnostics remain allowlisted and redacted inside the module; surface, target, source, renderer, binding, owner generation, path and raw exception content never cross Channel or enter logs.
A Native render surface or internal source cannot be replaced by media bytes, path, URI, descriptor, platform object, opaque token or untyped payload fallback.
thumbnailCopy uses only the Channel byte-array representation corresponding to Dart Uint8List.
thumbnailByteLength is 1 through 524288 and equals the actual thumbnailCopy byte length.
Thumbnail output is image/jpeg with physically upright pixels and thumbnailOrientationDegrees equal to zero.
The bounded copy contains no EXIF, location, device, source filename, or other non-display source metadata.
Thumbnail reads require a confirmed active lease, do not refresh lease/grace/TTL/tombstone, and never expose original media.
Photo posterFrameMillis is null; video returns the actual frame chosen by the Capability target/after/before/tie policy.
No source bytes, path, URI, file descriptor, untyped Map, SDK object, or fallback representation may replace the bounded thumbnail bytes.
Dart never supplies a path, URI, filename, descriptor, remote URL, shared-storage locator, or target directory for transfer materialization.
fileUri is Adapter-created under the plugin-owned app-private transfer root, has a fixed TTL, and is consumed only for immediate infrastructure import.
fileUri and exportHandle are sensitive local locators and never enter logs, error details, events, messages, fixtures, routes, analytics, or persistence.
Each Engine attachment permits at most four active exports and 104857600 active bytes; each file is capped at 52428800 bytes and overload does not invoke Capability.
Release, detach, restart, TTL, cancel, completion failure, and late Capability result delete or tombstone transfer files exactly once before drop.
Dart imports the materialized transfer before releasing the export and releases source media only after import succeeds.
Raw media bytes, chunks, descriptors, source paths, and caller-provided sinks never cross the Channel.

changeLog.description: Initial typed Media Capture mapping with bounded transport, typed error details, listener and host lifecycle policy, and direct Capability failure-emission coverage; callback-scoped native media reads are intentionally not exposed.

Adds a full-screen presentation method and sanitized bounded thumbnail bytes; Capability V3 module-defined render surfaces and internals remain Native-only, so the existing Version 2 Channel shape is unchanged while supporting Capability Versions 2 and 3.

Adds scoped one-time materialize and release methods for Capability V4 bounded export using an Adapter-owned private cache store, plus a request-correlated Adapter presentation dismiss method for Flutter lifecycle cleanup. Transfer uses 128-bit CSPRNG export handles, fixed native sink and length bindings, canonical short-lived file URI locators, closed media metadata, optional SHA-256 integrity, bounded tombstones, and ordered cleanup while preserving Wire V1/V2 history; dismiss is Android-supported and explicitly deferred on iOS.
